This looks like it modifies the type hints for the whole array. So all elements updated after may have the wrong hints with a mixed array.
Same applies for the equivalent changes in the dictionary section

If there's data intended to be `NodePath` in a mixed collection, this would be changing what the loaded values will be.

`p_should_bind_paths` should only be true for fixed type node collections to load `PackedScene`s made before this change in the same way.

```suggestion
// Recursively parses arrays, mostly to look for Nodes to turn into NodeBindings
```

Same with dictionary equivalent

Could flag the property as having `NodeBinding`s during `_parse_node` using `FLAG_PATH_PROPERTY_IS_NODE` instead of traversing the collections on instantiate. Then it'd be added to the deferred list in the same way as existing check and not have to run through the collection twice.

The conversions in the deferred update would need to call `make_local_resource` at the right places though.

Subtle issue: The original code calling `duplicate` on the return of `get` maintains collection types because the types are used for correctly duplicating node references in `Node::duplicate()` and `get` returns correctly typed collections based on property hints.

Potentially, but that's be something to address in a separate PR to keep this one focused on one issue. Just make sure the changes don't break anything with resources in the top level collection at least.

Could you clarify what you mean by "making sure the dictionary types are correct?"

The dictionary at the end should have the same types for the key and value as the dictionary returned by `get` on the Node by either calling `set_typed` or duplicating the dictionary from `get`. This is so the changes don't break `Node::duplicate()` as I mentioned before.

Same applies to arrays.

Looping over the output dictionary, so dictionaries aren't loading in with data from file.

Since it's the 3rd round of review, do you have a small test scene to check the regressions I've pointed out? Just a script that exports arrays/dictionaries that are typed for nodes, exports arrays/dictionaries with a mix of nodes, nodepaths, and resources, and exports arrays/dictionaries nested in various ways to run through open and save a couple times.
I'm curious because some of these issues would have been revealed in that testing. I apologize for getting off-topic, but these changes are affecting more than just the linked issue and require more testing than just that issue's mrp. While reviewers will be testing it, it saves time and rounds of review if you've tested as thoroughly as you can.
